clue.text: Religious tome's heartless anger

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letter, here the middle of five

parts.note: the Bible is the religious book of Christianity

explanation.surface: Someone notices the fury running through a sacred book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle B of BIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bile is a literary word for bitterness and irritable temper, from the old humour thought to cause it.

clue.text: Person with little time for Cornish town

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
min is short for minute, a little time

explanation.surface: Someone too busy to bother with a town in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: BODMIN is a town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodmin is a historic market town on the moor in Cornwall, England.

clue.text: Attack making one hide

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to pelt someone with stones, and a fox's pelt as its skin.

clue.text: Business programme in information carried by a US lawyer

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: DA is District Attorney, an American prosecutor
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A list of business is in the details an American attorney brings along.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items of business to be dealt with at a meeting.

clue.text: Bird featured in what is dull lecture for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners says the words are to be heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: grey means dull and a talk is a lecture

explanation.surface: A bird gets a mention in a tedious talk, as heard by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in what is' are link words; GREY TALK spoken sounds like the extinct bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The great auk was a large flightless seabird of the North Atlantic, hunted to extinction.

clue.text: Finish with copper getting mad, giving description of written evidence

parts.note: to do a task is to complete or finish it
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: Ending a job with a police officer losing his temper, someone gives an account of written proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'getting' are link words; 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Documental is an adjective meaning relating to or consisting of documents, the written evidence.

clue.text: One group wants attendant around to provide guidance

indicators.note: around says the attendant word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lot is a group or batch of items

explanation.surface: A party needs a helper nearby to show them the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilotage is the act of guiding a vessel, so the work of giving direction.

clue.text: Performer in a cape with long hair

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A performer appears in a cloak, hair flowing down.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who performs on stage or screen.

clue.text: General as fellow going after blood, no end

indicators.note: going after places the fellow word behind the blood word
no end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A general sees a fellow chasing bloodshed without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims GORE to GOR; GORDON was the British general killed at Khartoum.
explanation.definitionFit: General Charles Gordon was a celebrated Victorian army commander, killed at Khartoum in 1885.

clue.text: Some duffer mathematically? Yes and no!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Was someone a duffer at maths? Well, both yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the wordplay: the name is literally in 'duffer mathematically', yet the man was no mathematical duffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre de Fermat sits inside the duffer phrase, yes, but was a great mathematician, so no.

clue.text: Wicked king's army destroyed sultan

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of sultan are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A villainous monarch's troops have wiped out a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Tantalus was a king punished in Hades for his crimes against the gods.

clue.text: Magnificent residence with fantastic ambience a help, including lake

indicators.note: including puts the lake letter inside the rearranged letters
fantastic suggests something wildly reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A grand home with a wonderful atmosphere helps, especially with a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges AMBIENCEAHELP into BENHEIMPALACE; 'including' puts L after its B. Blenheim Palace is the Oxfordshire stately home where Churchill was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace is a vast baroque country house in Oxfordshire, seat of the Dukes of Marlborough.

clue.text: Thrashing could make hate linger

indicators.note: could make says the following letters can be rebuilt into something new

explanation.surface: A beating might leave resentment hanging around.
explanation.definitionFit: A leathering is British slang for a beating, as with a leather strap.

clue.text: State with sea to east

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A state lies with the ocean to its east.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Injury requires member to be seen by hospital

indicators.note: to be seen by says the limb word stands beside the hospital letter, following it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps
an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: A hurt limb needs looking at in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm means damage or hurt done to someone, an injury.

clue.text: Fellows embarrassed, about to get counselled

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go round the next word

parts.note: men are fellows
red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed

explanation.surface: Blushing men are about to receive advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mentored is to be guided and advised by an experienced adviser.

clue.text: Fielders making mistakes

definitions.meaning: cricket fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close fielders behind the batsman on the off side; 'making' just joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the slips cordon in cricket and slips as errors.

clue.text: Theologian perhaps affected by the sun when going outside church

indicators.note: going outside says the sun word wraps round the church letters

parts.note: solar means relating to or caused by the sun

explanation.surface: A divinity expert gets sunburnt when he leaves church.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologian is one example of a scholar, a learned academic.

clue.text: Bird — young cat gets the tail of one

parts.note: kit is short for kitten

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A kitten grabs the tail of one bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kite is a bird of prey with a forked tail.

clue.text: Diversion that could put the sewer temporarily out of action

definitions.text: Diversion that could put the sewer temporarily out of action

parts.words: Diversion that could put the sewer temporarily out of action
parts.note: sewer reads as a drain, but means someone who sews; a party game searching for the finger-guard would leave that person stuck

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drains; read sewer as a person who sews, whose finger protector has been hidden for a parlour game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian parlour game in which players search for a hidden needle-guard, so a diversion or pastime.

clue.text: Go short on food — nice things like chocolates?

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt
eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Someone eating little has goodies such as chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims TRY to TR; 'on' joins it to EATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Treats are small indulgences, and chocolates are a typical example of such pleasures.

clue.text: Poet's change of position

definitions.meaning: Andrew ... was the British Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009
movement from one place to another

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is the poet's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion is both a poet's surname and the general word for movement.

clue.text: Rare boat fashioned in various woods specially cultivated

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual boat made from a mix of carefully grown timbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreta are botanical gardens where many kinds of trees are grown for study and display.

clue.text: Supporter is silly guy losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: wally is British slang for a foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone's backer turns out to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone who supports and sides with another.

clue.text: Dormant a short time in period before Easter

indicators.note: in places the short pieces inside the period word

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of forty days before Easter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something lies quiet for a brief while during the weeks before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but hidden or inactive, like something dormant.

clue.text: Agent may have hurried up when getting cold

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ran means hurried
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spy might have dashed off when he caught a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics agent, an undercover drugs officer.

clue.text: Design of trendy shelter

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: The style of a fashionable marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent means purpose or aim, as does design in 'by design'.

clue.text: 'Left on ship' is about right!

indicators.note: is about says the first pieces surround the next letter

parts.note: aboard means on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that the old nautical term for port really means left.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: 'is about' puts R inside LABOARD after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical term for the port, or left-hand, side of a ship.
